cards.title: The English Tense System
rule: The English Tense System: Future & Perfect Aspects

Definition: The Future & Perfect Aspects (ናይ መጻኢን ፍጹም እዋናትን መልክዕ) refer to the grammatical structures used to describe completed actions connected to the present ($$\text{Present Perfect}$$), completed actions prior to a past point ($$\text{Past Perfect}$$), and various ways to express intentions, predictions, and schedules in the future.

Contrasting the Present Perfect ($$\text{Subject} + \text{have/has} + \text{V}_3$$) with the Simple Past ($$\text{Subject} + \text{V}_2$$) is a major focus of English syntax exams. Simple Past is strictly limited to actions completed at a definite, closed time in the past (e.g., *yesterday, in 2015, three days ago*). In contrast, Present Perfect describes actions that occurred at an indefinite, open time in the past, or actions that began in the past and continue to have direct relevance to the present. Tigrinya speakers often face challenges here because Tigrinya lacks a direct equivalent to the Present Perfect. Completed actions in Tigrinya are usually expressed using the gerundive verb aspect (e.g., "መጺኡ" - *he has come* or *he came*). This morphological overlap causes students to write errors like "I have seen him yesterday" because they translate the completed past state directly without applying the English rule of definite vs. indefinite time.

examples.text: She goes to school every day.
She go to school every day.
examples.fix: She goes to school every day.

cards.title: Notes
body: The English Tense System: Future & Perfect Aspects

Definition: The Future & Perfect Aspects (ናይ መጻኢን ፍጹም እዋናትን መልክዕ) refer to the grammatical structures used to describe completed actions connected to the present ($$\text{Present Perfect}$$), completed actions prior to a past point ($$\text{Past Perfect}$$), and various ways to express intentions, predictions, and schedules in the future.

Contrasting the Present Perfect ($$\text{Subject} + \text{have/has} + \text{V}_3$$) with the Simple Past ($$\text{Subject} + \text{V}_2$$) is a major focus of English syntax exams. Simple Past is strictly limited to actions completed at a definite, closed time in the past (e.g., *yesterday, in 2015, three days ago*). In contrast, Present Perfect describes actions that occurred at an indefinite, open time in the past, or actions that began in the past and continue to have direct relevance to the present. Tigrinya speakers often face challenges here because Tigrinya lacks a direct equivalent to the Present Perfect. Completed actions in Tigrinya are usually expressed using the gerundive verb aspect (e.g., "መጺኡ" - *he has come* or *he came*). This morphological overlap causes students to write errors like "I have seen him yesterday" because they translate the completed past state directly without applying the English rule of definite vs. indefinite time.

The Present Perfect relies on key time-markers (ናይ ግዜ መመልከቲታት) such as *already, yet, since, for, recently, so far, up to now, ever,* and *never*. A common exam topic is the distinction between since (which marks the exact starting point of a duration, e.g., "since 2010") and for (which marks the total length of the duration, e.g., "for ten years"). Tigrinya often uses the preposition "ካብ" (from) or time clauses in ways that blur this distinction (e.g., "ካብ 2010 ጀሚሩ" and "ንዓሰርተ ዓመት"), leading students to incorrectly write "since ten years" on exams.

cards.title: Talk about the future
cards.problem: Choose the best form: (a) "Look at those clouds! It ____ rain." (b) "I ____ meet the doctor at 10 tomorrow – it's booked." (c) "The phone is ringing." – "I ____ answer it."

steps.text: **Step 1: Prediction from present evidence → be going to.** (a) It's going to rain.
**Step 2: Fixed arrangement → present continuous.** (b) I'm meeting the doctor at 10.
**Step 3: Decision made at the moment of speaking → will.** (c) I'll answer it.
**Tip:** ask whether the future is evidence-based, arranged, or decided now.

cards.answer: (a) is going to rain; (b) am meeting; (c) will ('ll) answer.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Aster ________ in this biotechnology laboratory since she graduated from university five years ago.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The time-marker 'since she graduated' indicates an action that started in the past and continues to the present, requiring the Present Perfect Continuous tense ($$\text{S} + \text{has/have been} + \text{V-ing}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often see 'is working' (Option A) and choose it because they think of it as an ongoing present action. However, 'since' requires the perfect aspect, making 'has been working' (Option C) correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Since' (ካብቲ...) ዝብል ናይ ግዜ መመልከቲ ካብ ሕሉፍ ግዜ ጀሚሩ ክሳብ ሕጂ ዝቕጽል ተግባር ስለ ዝሕብር፡ እቲ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ኣብ Present Perfect Continuous ክስራዕ ኣለዎ። እቲ ዋና ባእታ 'Aster' (ነጸላ) ስለ ዝኾነ ድማ ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'has been working' (Option C) እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The construction company ________ the new highway road project three weeks ago.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The definite past time-marker 'three weeks ago' requires the Simple Past tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_2$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often confuse Present Perfect 'has completed' (Option A) with Simple Past 'completed' (Option B). Present Perfect cannot be used with definite past time-markers like 'three weeks ago'.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Three weeks ago' (ቅድሚ ሰለስተ ሰሙን) ዝብል ናይ ግዜ መመልከቲ ኣብ ሕሉፍ ግዜ ተፈጺሙ ምውድኡ ስለ ዝሕብር፡ እቲ ግሲ ብ Past Simple 'completed' (Option B) ክጸሓፍ ኣለዎ። Present Perfect ምስ 'ago' ክኸይድ ኣይኽእልን እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: My uncle is a manager in the Coca-Cola share company. He __________ there ever since he graduated from college.
cards.why: The phrase 'ever since' indicates an action that started in the past and is still continuing. Since the uncle is still a manager, the Present Perfect Continuous ('has been working') is the most appropriate.

games.title: Match the tense to its use

pairs.b: past action linked to now (since, for, yet)
the earlier of two past actions

questions.q: Aster ________ in this biotechnology laboratory since she graduated from university five years ago.
questions.label: 1. Aster ________ in this biotechnology laboratory since she gr
why: The time-marker 'since she graduated' indicates an action that started in the past and continues to the present, requiring the Present Perfect Continuous tense ($$\text{S} + \text{has/have been} + \text{V-ing}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The construction company ________ the new highway road project three weeks ago.
questions.label: 2. The construction company ________ the new highway road proje
why: The definite past time-marker 'three weeks ago' requires the Simple Past tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_2$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Look at those thick dark clouds hanging over the mountains! It ________ rain very soon.
questions.label: 3. Look at those thick dark clouds hanging over the mountains!
why: This is a future prediction based on clear, present physical evidence ('thick dark clouds'). This requires 'be going to' ($$\text{S} + \text{be going to} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: The public train to Djibouti ________ from the main station at exactly 7:30 AM tomorrow.
questions.label: 4. The public train to Djibouti ________ from the main station
why: The departure of a public train is a formal, timetabled future event that is outside of personal control. This requires the Present Simple tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_{\text{1/s/es}}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: By the time the guest speaker arrives at the hall tomorrow, the students ________ for over two hours.
questions.label: 5. By the time the guest speaker arrives at the hall tomorrow,
why: The time-marker 'By the time... tomorrow' paired with the durative marker 'for over two hours' requires the Future Perfect Continuous tense ($$\text{S} + \text{will have been} + \text{V-ing}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: I ________ to Axum twice, but I hope to visit its historical sites again next year.
questions.label: 6. I ________ to Axum twice, but I hope to visit its historical
why: This sentence describes a life experience at an indefinite past time, requiring the Present Perfect tense ($$\text{S} + \text{have/has} + \text{V}_3$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q:
Speaker A: 'The phone is ringing in the living room!' 
Speaker B: 'Don't worry, I ________ it.'
questions.label:
7. Speaker A: 'The phone is ringing in the living room!' 
Speak
why: This is a spontaneous decision made at the moment of speaking in response to an immediate situation. This requires the future auxiliary 'will' ($$\text{S} + \text{will} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: He ________ the historic manuscript for four hours, and his eyes are extremely tired now.
questions.label: 8. He ________ the historic manuscript for four hours, and his
why: The durative marker 'for four hours' and the present result 'his eyes are extremely tired now' require the Present Perfect Continuous tense ($$\text{S} + \text{has/have been} + \text{V-ing}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: We have lived in this historic neighborhood in Gondar ________ five years.
questions.label: 9. We have lived in this historic neighborhood in Gondar ______
why: 'Five years' is a length of duration. In English, durations of time require the preposition 'for' ($$\text{for} + \text{duration}$$).
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: My parents ________ the high school principal tomorrow afternoon to discuss my academic progress.
questions.label: 10. My parents ________ the high school principal tomorrow after
why: Meeting a principal 'tomorrow afternoon' is a confirmed personal arrangement with a fixed time and place, requiring the Present Continuous for future arrangement.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence before choosing.

questions.q: Aster ____ in this laboratory since 2019.
questions.label: 11. Aster ____ in this laboratory since 2019.

similar.q: Complete: I ____ (know) him for ten years.
Complete: They ____ (live) here since 2010.

why: "since 2019" shows an action from the past continuing to now.
Use the present perfect (or present perfect continuous).
questions.tip: Present perfect links past and now (since, for, already, yet, ever). Past perfect = earlier past. Future forms: will (decision/prediction), going to (plan/evidence), present continuous (arrangement).

questions.q: Look at those dark clouds! It ____ rain.
questions.label: 12. Look at those dark clouds! It ____ rain.

similar.q: Complete: Watch out! You ____ (fall).
Complete: She's pale; she ____ (faint).

why: The speaker sees present evidence (dark clouds).
Predictions based on evidence use "going to".
So: It is going to rain.
questions.tip: Present perfect links past and now (since, for, already, yet, ever). Past perfect = earlier past. Future forms: will (decision/prediction), going to (plan/evidence), present continuous (arrangement).

questions.q: "The phone is ringing." "I ____ answer it."
questions.label: 13. "The phone is ringing." "I ____ answer it."

similar.q: Respond: "It's cold in here."
Respond: "I've forgotten my pen."

why: The speaker decides at the moment of speaking.
"going to" is for decisions made earlier.
questions.tip: Present perfect links past and now (since, for, already, yet, ever). Past perfect = earlier past. Future forms: will (decision/prediction), going to (plan/evidence), present continuous (arrangement).

questions.q: By the time we reached the cinema, the film ____.
questions.label: 14. By the time we reached the cinema, the film ____.

similar.q: Complete: When I got home, my sister ____ (cook) dinner.
Complete: The plane ____ (take off) before we got to the airport.

why: The film started before we reached the cinema.
The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect.
questions.tip: Present perfect links past and now (since, for, already, yet, ever). Past perfect = earlier past. Future forms: will (decision/prediction), going to (plan/evidence), present continuous (arrangement).

questions.q: Correct the error: "I have finished my project last week."
questions.label: 15. Correct the error: "I have finished my project last week."

similar.q: Correct: He has arrived yesterday.
Correct: Have you seen the match last night?
similar.a: Did you see the match last night?

questions.answer: I finished my project last week.
why: "last week" is a finished past time.
The present perfect cannot be used with finished times.
questions.tip: Present perfect links past and now (since, for, already, yet, ever). Past perfect = earlier past. Future forms: will (decision/prediction), going to (plan/evidence), present continuous (arrangement).

questions.q: By next year, she ____ her degree.
questions.label: 16. By next year, she ____ her degree.

similar.q: Complete: By 6 p.m. I ____ (finish).
Complete: By 2030 the road ____ (build).

why: "By next year" refers to an action finished before a future time.
Future perfect: will have + past participle.
questions.tip: Present perfect links past and now (since, for, already, yet, ever). Past perfect = earlier past. Future forms: will (decision/prediction), going to (plan/evidence), present continuous (arrangement).

questions.q: Read: "Daniel has been learning Italian for two years. He has already visited Rome once, and next summer he is spending a month in Milan with a host family." What arrangement does Daniel have for next summer?
questions.label: 17. Read: "Daniel has been learning Italian for two years. He has already visited Rome once, and next…

similar.q: How long has Daniel been learning Italian?
Which tense shows his experience of Rome?

options.D: He is spending a month in Milan.

why: Answer D: He is spending a month in Milan.
"next summer he is spending a month in Milan" uses the present continuous for a fixed arrangement.
The other options describe past or ongoing actions.
So the arrangement is the month in Milan.
questions.tip: Present perfect links past and now (since, for, already, yet, ever). Past perfect = earlier past. Future forms: will (decision/prediction), going to (plan/evidence), present continuous (arrangement).

questions.q: She ____ for three hours when the doctor finally arrived.
questions.label: 18. She ____ for three hours when the doctor finally arrived.

similar.q: Complete: They ____ (walk) for hours before they found water.
Complete: I'm tired; I ____ (study) all morning.

why: The waiting continued up to a past moment (the doctor arrived).
Present forms do not fit the past context.
questions.tip: Present perfect links past and now (since, for, already, yet, ever). Past perfect = earlier past. Future forms: will (decision/prediction), going to (plan/evidence), present continuous (arrangement).

questions.q: Have you ____ been to Nakfa?
questions.label: 19. Have you ____ been to Nakfa?

similar.q: Complete: I have ____ (never / ever) seen snow.
Complete: Have you finished ____?

why: "ever" is used with the present perfect in questions about experience.
"yet" goes at the end; "since" and "ago" do not fit here.
questions.tip: Present perfect links past and now (since, for, already, yet, ever). Past perfect = earlier past. Future forms: will (decision/prediction), going to (plan/evidence), present continuous (arrangement).

questions.q: True or false: "We are meeting the principal at 10 tomorrow" describes a fixed arrangement.
questions.label: 20. True or false: "We are meeting the principal at 10 tomorrow" describes a fixed arrangement.

similar.q: Arrangement: (I / fly to Cairo / on Friday)
similar.a: I'm flying to Cairo on Friday.

similar.q: Instant decision: "I ____ (help) you carry that."

why: True. The present continuous with a future time expression shows an arrangement already made.
Both people know about the meeting.
questions.tip: Present perfect links past and now (since, for, already, yet, ever). Past perfect = earlier past. Future forms: will (decision/prediction), going to (plan/evidence), present continuous (arrangement).
